title: Fence Painting & Staining in Archer, FL
description: Fence painting and staining in Archer, FL for board fences on ranches, privacy fences, and gates. Wash, repair, then stain or paint. Free written estimates.
h1: Fence Painting and Staining in Archer, FL
heroIntro: From a privacy fence around a backyard in Holly Hills to long board-fence runs on a ranch, we clean, repair, and coat fencing so it holds up to Archer sun and rain.

questions: Should I paint or stain my wood fence in Archer?
How long does it take to stain a long fence line?
Can you paint a vinyl fence?

body: Fencing around Archer runs from short backyard privacy fences in the subdivisions to long runs of board fence along driveways and paddocks on ranch land. The longer the line, the more it matters that the coating is chosen once and done right, because nobody wants to redo a quarter mile of boards every other summer.

Fences get abuse a house never sees: sprinklers hitting the same boards daily, sand splashing the bottom rail, vines and weeds holding moisture against posts, and full sun on both faces. Our fence painting in Archer, FL starts by looking at those conditions on your line.

Gates deserve special mention. They swing, sag, and get grabbed every day, so we check hinges and latches, re-fasten loose boards, and give gate faces a little extra attention. A gate that drags on the ground will wick moisture into its bottom rail no matter how good the coating is, so we flag it during the walkthrough.

sections.h2: Paint or stain? A quick guide
bullets: Previously painted fences: usually stay painted; we scrape, spot-prime bare wood, and apply 100% acrylic
Bare, weathered, or previously stained wood: penetrating stain, which soaks in and will not peel
Mismatched boards from repairs: solid stain or paint evens them out
Vinyl fencing: cleaned and, where sound, coated with a product rated for vinyl
body: Stain is often the easier long-term choice on rural board fencing, since it weathers away rather than peeling and can be refreshed without scraping.

Not sure which camp your fence falls into? The crew lead can test-scrape a few boards during the walkthrough. If you also want a matching color for posts, gates, or a nearby shed, our Archer color consultation can tie them together.

sections.h2: Prep before a single board is coated
body: We wash the fence to remove mildew, dirt, and gray surface fibers, then let it dry. Loose boards are re-fastened and broken or rotted pickets and rails are replaced. Peeling paint is scraped back to a sound edge. Vegetation along the base is pulled back, and plants and the ground are protected from overspray. Stain is sprayed and then back-brushed so it penetrates rough-sawn faces and end grain.
Sun-grayed and splitting wood is common here; our guide on treating sun-damaged fences in Alachua County explains what can be saved.

Fence work wants dry wood and a dry forecast, so fall through spring is best. Long runs are measured during the walkthrough so the estimate reflects the true footage. Many owners pair the fence with deck staining in Archer since the prep and products overlap. See our main deck and fence staining page for product details.

faqs.q: Do you stain long board fences on ranch property?
faqs.a: Yes. We measure the full run at the walkthrough and price it as its own line, so you can do the whole line or phase it.
Penetrating stain soaks into the wood rather than forming a surface film, so it fades over time instead of peeling.

faqs.q: Can you replace broken pickets before painting?
faqs.a: Yes. Board replacement and re-fastening are part of prep and are listed on your estimate.
